content:
When Apple finally responded to the sharp rise in memory and other component costs, its stance was quite tough. Some products saw price hikes exceeding fifty percent, while certain memory and storage upgrade options saw prices double outright.

These elevated prices are likely to remain for years, and may never come back down...

9to5Mac readers have long been skeptical about whether Apple would cut prices once component supply constraints eased. Over two-thirds of readers said they expected these price increases to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report indicated that supply chain pricing would not improve in any meaningful way before 2028, and even if changes come then, they would be quite limited. The current extremely high pricing will persist for at least several years, and may well never return to previous levels — the situation seems quite clear.

If this turns out to be the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue buying Apple products at the same pace? Or would you cut back on the quantity or frequency of purchases? Or take other approaches, such as choosing lower-tier models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a move?

Feel free to take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections to reflect the various ways you might adjust your purchasing behavior.
